Genegoggle is a precision medicine biotech company with the goal of discovering novel therapeutics and intelligent systems to improve human health by leveraging multi-dimensional genomic and epigenetic elements. We apply interdisciplinary expertise and multi-omic strategies to precision medicine and chronic diseases on the Earth and beyond.
We are focused on epigenetic mechanisms of gene expression regulation and the packaging of the DNA chain in the cell nucleus. We identify intracellular processes that can be used for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. We are particularly interested in the regulatory modes triggered by extracellular factors like medical treatments or modified environments.

At Genegoggle our mission is to enhance the understanding of the human genome and provide tools to support human health. Our personalized approach is powered by artificial intelligence. Our team gathers deep expertise in epigenetics, computational biology, machine learning, and software engineering, and data visualization to mark new directions in medical genomics.

The Foundation's main purpose is to combat and mitigate human-induced climate change using solutions based on nature and pursue civic, solidarity and social utility purposes. The Foundation's activity is divided into the following activities.
Arboreal Plant Projects
These are projects that create arboreal plants in previously not wooded areas or arboreal plants in areas where the forest has been cleared by natural or anthropogenic disturbances.
Sustainable Forest Management Projects
These are projects aimed at enhancing the storage of carbon in the forest, at mitigating or preventing the effects of natural disturbances and at increasing the resistance and resilience of forest stands to climate change.
Supply Chain Projects
These are projects aimed at enhancing local supply chains and the efficient use of resources from the point of view of the effects on the climate from a bioeconomy and circular economy perspective.
Research and Transfer Projects
These are projects that aim to improve and transfer knowledge on the techniques for designing, planting and maintaining trees in urban and rural environments, on the benefits they generate, on the response of trees and forests to environmental stress factors and the effects of climate crisis. The Foundation develops on a scientific basis tools to support decisions for the implementation of plant, sustainable management and supply chain projects.
Promotion, Training and Communication Projects
Activities aimed at disseminating knowledge based on the best science available to technicians, administrators and citizens regarding the Foundation's objectives and support for governance policies of local territories.

Ovidius” University of Constanta (www.univ-ovidius.ro) is the leading Academic institution from the South-East Region of Romania. The 15.000 students of OUC are registered in 16 faculties, covering a wide range of subjects, from life sciences and humanities to engineering and fundamental sciences. Being structured as a classical European university, OUC is playing an active regional role with strong ties with the business and social communities.
The Institute for Nanotechnologies and Alternative Energy Sources (INAES) is an autonomous research institute established in 2011 by the OUC Senate in order to bridge the gap between scientific research and education activities carried out in the university with the needs for innovation, technology development and smart specializations from the regional economy. 
The mission of INAES is to achieve excellence in scientific research, master and doctoral programs, helping to promote innovation as a determining factor in increasing regional competitiveness and sustainable development. The research projects developed by the INAES cover a wide range of fields, in an interdisciplinary approach, structured on 4 main topics: sustainable energy solutions, materials and nanotechnologies, multiscale modelling, simulation and sustainable transport systems.
The research team involved in the current project covers competencies related to experimental investigations, modelling and simulation, engineering, renewable energy sources, biology-environment, life cycle assessment.
At the same time, the research teams of INAES are developing cooperative activities under the frame of the Black Sea Universities Network (BSUN) - a network of more than 120 universities from the Black Sea Region (www.bsun.org).

entityDescription:
The Ferdinand-Braun-Institut gGmbH, Leibniz-Institut fuer Hoechstfrequenztechnik (FBH) researches electronic and optical components, modules and systems based on compound semiconductors. These devices are key enablers that address the needs of today’s society in fields like communications, energy, health, and mobility. Specifically, FBH develops light sources from the visible to the ultra-violet spectral range: high-power diode lasers with excellent beam quality, UV light sources and hybrid laser modules. Applications range from medical technology, high-precision metrology and sensors to optical communications in space and integrated quantum technology. In the field of microwaves, FBH develops high-efficiency multi-functional power amplifiers and millimeter wave frontends targeting energy-efficient mobile communications, industrial sensing and imaging as well as car safety systems. In addition, high-speed laser drivers are fabricated for use in a variety of applications.
The FBH is a center of competence for III-V compound semiconductors covering the full range of capabilities, from design through fabrication to device characterization. Within Research Fab Microelectronics Germany (Forschungsfabrik Mikroelektronik Deutschland), FBH joins forces with 12 other German research institutes, thus offering the complete micro and nanoelectronics value chain as a one-stop-shop.
In close cooperation and strategic partnerships with industry, FBH's research results lead to cutting-edge products. The institute also successfully turns innovative product ideas into spin-off companies. With its Prototype Engineering Lab, the institute strengthens its cooperation with customers in industry by turning excellent research results into market-oriented products, processes, and services. The institute thereby offers its international customer base complete solutions and know-how as a one-stop agency – from design to ready-to-use modules and prototypes.

The Consortium has two sites: in Roma and Genova. The president is Gian Carlo Cardarilli, full professor of Digital Electronics and Electronics for Communication Systems at the University of Rome Tor Vergata.
